equity_bridge.note: 8-K 2026-09-10 merger agreement; SC TO-T 2026-09-17; ~1.9bn per announcement

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: revenue 3yr CAGR (6.4%) haircut for FY26's +0.4% and US unit share loss; equity CAGR rejected
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 20.8% diverges >30% from revenue 3yr 6.4% and EPS 3yr 6.0%. Book growth is retained cash (net cash rose from ~0.65bn FY21 to 4.5bn FY26 while ~no buybacks until FY26), not business growth, so the equity CAGR is not used as the growth anchor.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF deducts SBC incl. withholding taxes and, from FY2023 (first net-interest-income year), interest income: FY23 65.9m, FY24 145.7m, FY25 178.9m, FY26 181.9m (XBRL InterestIncomeExpenseNonoperatingNet; FY21-22 were net expense, nothing deducted). The owner-FCF CAGR runs ~2pp below reported, and that gap is the growing interest income, not SBC: SBC is flat at ~0.8-1.0% of revenue. FY26 FCF is flattered by 7.2% capex (vs 12-14%) and depressed by an 80m receivables build and 97m of tax receivable/payable swings. Revenue growth decelerated from 30% (FY22) to 0.4% (FY26).

scenario_narratives.base: Copart standalone stabilises: US insurance units flatten after FY26's ~-2.8% as the Progressive reallocation to IAA annualises, while ASP gains and the international segment (units +10%, revenue +11.7% in Q4 FY26) bring revenue growth back to ~5% before fading to 3%. Margin recovers only partially (41% pre-SBC EBITDA vs 42-44% in FY22-24) because IAA has closed the cycle-time gap. Capex normalises to ~10% of revenue then tapers. ACV is valued at its unaffected market price in the bridge, so the ~0.59bn premium is charged as value paid away.
scenario_narratives.bull: The secular total-loss-frequency tailwind (repair-cost inflation from ADAS/electronics outrunning used-vehicle values) reasserts itself, Copart's land bank and catastrophe surge capacity win back insurer share, and international becomes a second engine. Automation takes pre-SBC EBITDA margin back to ~43.5%. Growth peaks at 7.5% and fades to 3.5%, 20x exit.
scenario_narratives.bear: The moat erodes into a price-competitive duopoly: IAA's turnaround (cycle times ~7 days shorter, backlog -20%) keeps winning national-carrier assignments, Copart cuts fees to hold volume, revenue shrinks in FY27 and grows ~3% thereafter, and margin settles at 36.5%. Used-car price normalisation cuts ASP-linked fees. ACV turns into a multi-year drag (not in the flows). 15x exit.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Owner-FCF DCF on a strict owner basis: SBC and withholding taxes expensed, share count flat, interest income stripped with the 4.5bn cash and HTM portfolio added in the bridge, and the pending all-cash ACV purchase charged at its premium over ACV's unaffected value. The key judgment is margin: whether the Q4 FY26 compression (pre-SBC EBITDA 38% vs 42-44% historically) is the new competitive equilibrium with a resurgent IAA or a transitory mix and G&A effect.
key_risks_to_valuation: National-carrier concentration: further reallocations like Progressive's to IAA would push results toward the bear path
Margin: the 41% base recovery assumes the Q4 FY26 compression partly reverses; if 38% is the new level, base value falls materially
ACV: valued at unaffected market value with no synergies; losses beyond management's 'breakeven year one' guidance are not modelled
Capex normalisation: FY26's 7.2% capex flatters reported FCF; a return to FY22-FY25's 12-14% land-bank spend would cut owner FCF by ~200-300m/yr
Used-vehicle price cycle: ASP-linked fees and purchased-vehicle margins are cyclical
Interest income on the cash pile (~182m/yr) is excluded from flows; the value is carried as cash, so deploying it below the 9% WACC (as ACV's premium suggests) destroys value relative to this model

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 26.81-45.89
data_sources.financials: FY2026 (year ended 2026-07-31): Q4 FY2026 earnings release, 8-K Ex 99.1 filed 2026-09-10 (statements in thousands). FY2009-Q3 FY2026: CPRT_Metrics.csv / core_metrics (SEC XBRL). Interest income, withholding taxes and cash history: SEC XBRL companyfacts (CIK 900075). Share count cross-check: Q3 FY2026 10-Q cover (925.8m at 2026-05-27).
data_sources.qualitative: CPRT_Analysis.json (2026-09-26); ACV merger agreement 8-K and SC TO-T tender offer (2026-09-10 / 2026-09-17).

inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 Q4 earnings release (8-K Ex 99.1, 2026-09-10) cash flow statement: stock-based compensation 38,818k + payments for employee stock-based tax withholdings 3,736k (financing). Copart publishes no combined adjusted-EBITDA SBC line, so the two are summed. Filing units are thousands; converted to millions.
inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: Q4 FY2026 diluted weighted-average shares 932.14m (earnings release). Cross-check: basic shares outstanding 925.81m at 2026-05-27 (Q3 10-Q cover) with no Q4 repurchases (FY buyback 1,632.5m equals the 9M figure), plus ~6m option dilution. Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows. The FY2026 buyback (1.63bn, ~4.5% of the count) is value-neutral in this model; the ACV deal is all-cash, so no acquisition-currency issuance.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate. 10y UST ~4.3% + beta ~0.95 x 5.0% ERP = ~9.0%. No debt, so WACC = cost of equity. Same 9% in all scenarios: risk is charged through the probability-weighted driver paths, not a per-scenario premium.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP operating leases: lease cost sits inside facility operations, i.e. inside EBITDA. Lease liabilities (88.4m) therefore excluded from net debt. One treatment, not two. Copart owns most of its yard land, so leases are immaterial.
inputs.nci_treatment: Redeemable non-controlling interest 16.6m (July 2026 balance sheet) deducted in the equity bridge; NCI share of losses (-3.9m FY26) is immaterial to the flows.
inputs.net_cash_note: Net cash = cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash 1,907.9m + held-to-maturity securities (current) 2,581.9m - zero borrowings = 4,489.8m at 2026-07-31. Interest income (181.9m FY26) is stripped from the FCF base and excluded from the component build so the cash pile is counted once, in the bridge.
inputs.acv_treatment: Pending acquisition of ACV Auctions (merger agreement 2026-09-10; cash tender at $10.50/share, SC TO-T filed 2026-09-17, no financing condition, close expected by calendar year-end 2026). The user brief described it as cash+stock; the merger agreement and tender offer show it is ALL CASH, funded from the balance sheet. It is material (~42% of net cash, ~7% of market cap), so it is reflected in the equity bridge rather than the flows: deduct the ~1.9bn consideration and add ACV at its UNAFFECTED market value (~1.31bn, back-solved from the disclosed ~45% premium), i.e. the model charges the ~0.59bn premium as value paid away and credits nothing for synergies. ACV's revenue and losses are NOT in the driver paths (management guides breakeven contribution in year one, accretion from FY2028), so FY27 revenue growth is Copart standalone. Bull case upside from synergies and bear case downside from further ACV losses are described in the narratives but, because the bridge is global, not modelled per scenario.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (dcf-methods routing row 1/2: operating company, US, fee-based marketplace; no bank/REIT/holdco features; the HTM portfolio is corporate treasury, not a lending book). First valuation of CPRT (no MEMORY entry, no prior DCF). FY0 = FY2026 (year ended 31 July 2026) taken from the 2026-09-10 earnings release because the Metrics CSV stops at Q3 FY2026 and the FY2026 10-K is not yet filed; the release's statements are in thousands and were converted. FY26: revenue 4,666.2m (+0.4%), operating income 1,652.6m, D&A 229.4m (facility 201.7 + G&A 27.7), SBC 38.8m, so pre-SBC EBITDA 1,920.8m = 41.2% (FY25 42.0%, FY24 42.4%, FY23 43.6%; Q4 FY26 alone 38.2%). OCF 1,604.5m, capex 337.4m (7.2% of revenue, unusually low vs 12-14% FY22-FY25 land-bank years; a further 6.2m of capex was settled from deposits). Reported FCF 1,267.1m; owner FCF = 1,267.1 - 42.6 SBC incl. withholding - 181.9 interest income = 1,042.7m. The component build does not carry FY26's low capex forward: capex is modelled at 10% of revenue near-term, tapering. Buybacks: 1.63bn in FY26 after none FY20-FY25, so the flat count is being funded by a repurchaser. Data gaps in core_metrics (cash after FY2022, interest income after FY2020, all of FY2026) were filled from SEC XBRL companyfacts and the earnings release, not backfilled into the CSV (US filer; XBRL route owns that).

bear.narrative: The duopoly turns price-competitive: IAA's operational turnaround and the Progressive shift spread to other national carriers, US units keep falling and Copart concedes seller fees to hold volume. Pre-SBC EBITDA margin settles at 36.5% (Q4 FY26 was 38.2% with gross profit -5.5%), a 15x exit for a structurally slower business. Used-car price normalisation hits ASP-linked fees and purchased-vehicle margins. ACV's losses running beyond FY2027 would be further downside not captured in the flows.

base.narrative: Copart standalone. US insurance units stabilise after the FY26 decline as Progressive's reallocation to IAA annualises; pricing (ASP) and international (+10% units) carry growth back to ~5% mid-decade, fading to 3%. Pre-SBC EBITDA margin starts at 39.5% (FY26 41.2%, Q4 run-rate 38.2%) and recovers only to 41% on automation, below the 42-44% of FY22-FY24. Capex normalises to 10% of revenue (FY26's 7.2% not carried forward) and tapers to 8% as land-bank build slows.

bull.narrative: Total-loss frequency keeps rising (ADAS/electronics repair cost vs used-car values), Copart wins back share from IAA on cycle time and buyer depth, and the international export network (38% of units, 46% of dollars to international buyers) compounds at double digits. Automation lifts pre-SBC EBITDA margin back to the FY24 level (~43.5%). Capex stays higher to fund the growth. ACV synergies (cross-sell to dealers, shared logistics) would add to this but are not in the flows.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 18x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25%: FY26 brought measurable share loss to IAA (units -2.8% vs IAA +4.7%), a Q4 profitability miss (operating income -10.6%), and concentration in a handful of national carriers, one of which (Progressive) has already shifted volume. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs several independent things to go right (share regained, margin back to FY24, international compounding). Base held at 50%. The balance sheet (4.5bn net cash, no debt) rules out a solvency tail, so bear is margin compression, not distress.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
sanity_check.fy_end_month_source: December (fallback: no fiscal_year_end and no annual filing)
